description: nf-core/fastqrepair samplesheet context, aligned to the pinned 1.0.0 schemas. Recovers corrupted gzipped FASTQ files.

casava.help: Input read names follow the CASAVA 1.8+ convention.

dropunpaired.help: Discard reads whose mate is missing instead of writing them to a separate file.

pipeline.name: nf-core/fastqrepair
pipeline.core_rule: Columns are sample, fastq_1, fastq_2. sample and fastq_1 are required. Note the patterns accept UNCOMPRESSED .fastq as well as .gz, which is unusual and deliberate: a corrupted archive is the input.
pipeline.reference_requirement: NONE. The 1.0.0 schema declares no genome/fasta/gtf — it never aligns anything.

validation_rules: Do NOT pass --genome, --fasta or --gtf: the 1.0.0 schema declares none of them.
This is a repair step, not an analysis. Its output is fixed FASTQ files to feed another pipeline.
Do not run it routinely. Reach for it when a pipeline has failed on unreadable or desynchronised input.
The repaired reads are NOT the original data. If the files are already deposited, keep the deposit and the repair distinct.
notes: Always technically runnable on any FASTQ we hold, but it is a remedy rather than an analysis. Its output would be a derived dataset; think carefully before registering repaired reads as a new sample rather than as a fix to an existing one.

sources.label: nf-core/fastqrepair nextflow_schema.json @ 1.0.0
sources.notes: Authoritative: no required params beyond input/outdir; no reference options at all.

sources.label: nf-core/fastqrepair assets/schema_input.json @ 1.0.0
sources.notes: Authoritative columns: sample and fastq_1 required; the pattern permits uncompressed .fastq.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/fastqrepair input samplesheet.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Build an nf-core/fastqrepair sheet for D.SEQ records whose FASTQ files will not read.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected after another pipeline has failed on corrupted or desynchronised input.
population_priority: Confirm the files are actually damaged before running this.
One row per affected D.SEQ leaf.
final_checks: The user understands the output is a repaired copy, not the original.
